correction: Believed bluefinctl's tag-only stable/testing map ({stable: testing, latest: testing, lts: lts-testing, lts-hwe: lts-hwe-testing}) could be lifted verbatim. Verified reality: it targets two image references that do not exist. The mapping must be keyed on the registry path, not the tag alone.
evidence: GHCR manifest requests 2026-08-17: ghcr.io/ublue-os/bluefin:testing -> 404, ghcr.io/projectbluefin/bluefin-lts:lts-testing -> 404, while ghcr.io/ublue-os/bluefin:lts-testing -> 200 and ghcr.io/projectbluefin/bluefin-lts:testing -> 200. Recorded in internal/imageinfo/imageinfo.go's imageChannelMap comment and guarded by TestTargetTagUsesThePerImageTable.

correction: Believed gating a test-only image-descriptor override on --dry-run made it safe to ship, on the grounds that dry-run prevents mutation. Verified reality: dry-run gates mutations, not display, so a released binary would still misreport which image the machine runs. The override belongs behind a build tag absent from every shipped binary.
evidence: strings build/chairlift | grep -c CHAIRLIFT_IMAGE_INFO returns 0 for the untagged build and 1 under -tags chairlift_e2e; guarded by TestDescriptorOverrideStaysBehindTheE2EBuildTag.

correction: Believed listing installed Flatpaks as a flat ID set was sufficient for gaming mode. Verified reality: it made Disable attempt user-scope uninstalls of components the image preinstalled system-wide, reporting them to the user as failures for something ChairLift never installed. Scope must be tracked per component.
evidence: TestDisableSkipsSystemScopeComponentsInsteadOfFailingOnThem in internal/gaming/gaming_test.go.

correction: Believed `make test` ran the suite, as AGENTS.md documented it (`go test ./...`). Verified reality: `test` was absent from `.PHONY` while the repository carries a `test/` directory, so make treated the target as already satisfied — `make test` printed "'test' is up to date", ran nothing, and exited 0. `fmt` and `lint` were equally undeclared and escaped only because no directory shares their names.
evidence: `make test` output before the fix; `make -d -n test` decision lines. Fixed by declaring the full target inventory .PHONY and gated by internal/installcheck.TestMakefilePhonyCoversEveryTarget, whose negative control (removing `test` from .PHONY) exits 1 naming `test`.

correction: Believed a cask's install receipt lives at <prefix>/Caskroom/<token>/INSTALL_RECEIPT.json, mirroring the Cellar keg layout. Verified reality: Homebrew writes it one level deeper, at <prefix>/Caskroom/<token>/.metadata/INSTALL_RECEIPT.json, because Cask::Tab.create sets tabfile = cask.metadata_main_container_path/FILENAME and metadata_main_container_path is caskroom_path.join(".metadata"). PR #107 read the shallow path and wrote its fixtures there too, so the suite stayed green while cask-to-tap attribution would have returned an empty map on every real host.
evidence: Homebrew Library/Homebrew/cask/tab.rb and cask/metadata.rb; corrected in internal/homebrew/trust.go (see its doc comment naming .metadata/INSTALL_RECEIPT.json) and in trust_test.go's fixtures before #107 merged.

correction: Believed a digest obtained from `curl -sI <registry>/manifests/latest` was a sufficient pin for a container image. Verified reality: that request returns the per-architecture CHILD manifest digest, not the multi-arch index digest. PR #127 pinned all four RamaLama images to amd64 children. CI's [amd64, arm64] matrix only cross-compiles and would not have caught it; the breakage lands on arm64 hosts at runtime, where podman reports no matching manifest for linux/arm64 for an image the tag resolves fine on amd64.
evidence: quay.io manifest requests 2026-09-18 with Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json returned mediaType manifest.list for each image, and the PR's original digests appeared as .manifests[] amd64 entries of those indexes. Repinned to the index digests before merge; shape guarded by TestEveryStackIsPinnedByAnImmutableDigest.

correction: Believed `gh pr merge --disable-auto` was the way to remove a pull request from the merge queue, and inferred from its `disablePullRequestAutoMerge` error that no dequeue existed. Verified reality: that subcommand only cancels auto-merge; the merge queue has a real escape hatch in the GraphQL `dequeuePullRequest` mutation, and the call failed only because #127's merge had already completed. Irreversibility begins when the queue completes the merge, not when the pull request is enqueued.
evidence: GitHub GraphQL schema introspection lists enqueuePullRequest and dequeuePullRequest as Mutation fields; `gh pr merge 127 --disable-auto` failed against an already-merged pull request during the 2026-09-18 triage session.
promoted_to: docs/skills/factory-onboarding/SKILL.md; AGENTS.md Project Bluefin factory section

correction: Believed a coverage delta quoted in a pull request body described the project's gate. Verified reality: three agent-authored coverage PRs (#122, #125, #134) measured with a bare `go test -cover`, which counts tests CI never runs. Under the real filter `-run "^Test[^I]" -skip "Integration"` the deltas were internal/bootc 68.2->79.5 (claimed 76.8->95.5), internal/stageexec 78.4->80.4 (claimed 73.0->82.5), internal/homebrew 73.2->85.2 (claimed 73.2->85.5), internal/sysupdate 69.7->83.2 (claimed 73.9->95.8). Codecov consumes the filtered profile.
evidence: Re-measured per package with the gated command and a baseline taken by removing the new test file; several of the counted tests were named TestIsBootcBooted*/TestIsInstalled* and were excluded by the filter entirely.

correction: Believed the TestI-prefix accident was a hazard agents occasionally hit in new work. Verified reality: nine tests already in the tree are excluded by the filter CI currently applies, so no gate selects them — TestIsInstalledReflectsPATH (distrobox), three TestInstalledApplications* (gaming), three TestIsNativeAB* (sysupdate), TestInfoReturnsVersionOnly (version), and TestGoreleaserPublishesSystemIntegrationPackage (installcheck). The last is the test AGENTS.md and ADR-0006 both cite as enforcing the system-integration package split, so a documented invariant was unenforced. Also corrected: AGENTS.md read as permitting reserved names anywhere, but no enforced gate runs ./internal/... unfiltered and `make e2e` runs only ./test/e2e, so a reserved name under internal/ is executed by no gate at all; only the local `make test` convenience target runs those packages unfiltered, which is why the shape passes a developer's own run.
evidence: grep for '^func TestI' and '^func Test.*Integration' under internal/ returned nine matches; all nine renamed and now pass under the gated command. Gated by internal/installcheck.TestNoInternalTestNameIsExcludedByTheCIFilter, whose negative control (restoring TestInfoReturnsVersionOnly) exits 1 naming the file and test.

correction: Believed CompareVersions only needed custom segment-based parsing with tilde support for RPM versions. Verified reality: RPM requires EVR parsing with explicit epoch comparison (defaulting to implicit 0), and caret (^) semantics where snapshots sort after empty base versions but before any other character/segment. Without EVR and caret handling, caret snapshots (e.g. 2.0^20250611 vs 2.0.1) and epoch-bearing versions (e.g. 1:1.0 vs 2.0) are misclassified, inverting upgrade vs downgrade directions in staged diffs.
evidence: RPM librpm source rpmio/rpmvercmp.cc and rpmio/rpmver.cc; verified with internal/sbom.TestCompareVersions and TestDiffEVROrderingAndCaretSemantics in issue #64.

correction: Believed a successful (nil error) response from updex.Client.Features() meant updex features were configured and available. Verified reality: Updex returns an empty slice with nil error when no feature definitions exist on the system. ChairLift must require at least one feature (len(features) > 0) to treat Updex as installed, otherwise it shows the System Features group and allows update attempts without any configured features.
evidence: Issue #77; updex.IsInstalled() in internal/updex/updex.go; guarded by TestUpdexAvailabilityRequiresNonEmptyFeatures in internal/updex/updex_test.go.

correction: Believed Updex check failures would return a top-level error and that an empty results slice meant a feature had no components to update and should be skipped. Verified reality: Updex emits warnings via its progress reporter and returns an empty results slice with nil error when per-component manifest/version lookups fail. ChairLift must retain progress warnings, present an update check failed subtitle on features with empty results, and surface an incomplete state in the group description rather than claiming all features are up to date.
evidence: Issue #78; internal/updex/updex.go; internal/views/featurestatus/featurestatus.go; guarded by TestCheckFeaturesReturnsResultsAndRetainsWarnings in internal/updex/updex_test.go and TestFeatureWithZeroComponentsReportsFailedCheck in internal/views/featurestatus/featurestatus_test.go.

correction: Believed the gaming stack was six Flatpak applications, so one inventory built from `flatpak list --app` in both scopes could classify all of them. Verified reality: MangoHud is published as org.freedesktop.Platform.VulkanLayer.MangoHud, a Vulkan-layer extension of the freedesktop Platform runtime, and `--app`/`--runtime` are mutually exclusive `flatpak list` filters — the application listing never reports it however it was installed. It was therefore classified missing on every refresh, so Enable reinstalled it each run and Disable never removed the user-scope ref ChairLift had put there (issue #75).
evidence: internal/gaming/gaming.go listed it beside five app IDs while internal/flatpak.listApplications passed `--app` unconditionally; fixed by adding flatpak.Kind plus ListUser/SystemRuntimes and keying gaming's Scope on Ref{Kind, ID}. Guarded by TestGamingInventorySeesAUserInstalledRuntimeExtension, TestDisableRemovesTheUserScopeRuntimeExtension, and TestMangoHudIsModelledAsARuntimeExtension.
promoted_to: docs/design/overview.md gaming section; docs/design/package-managers.md Flatpak section

correction: Believed asserting that E2E-only stub variables were not read across a fixed list of six source files was sufficient to prevent production spoofing. Verified reality: moving or adding a stub variable read to any other Go source file in the untagged tree could ship in release binaries while the gate stayed green. The guard must walk the whole repository, evaluate build constraints across architectures, and ensure stubbed variables are permitted exclusively in the tagged override file.
evidence: TestDescriptorOverrideStaysBehindTheE2EBuildTag in internal/installcheck/channels_test.go; negative control adding spoof.go with os.Getenv("CHAIRLIFT_IMAGE_INFO") failed the updated walk but passed the legacy fixed list.

correction: Believed GoReleaser's per-format nfpms overrides merged over base fields by appending, so a base-level dependencies list plus per-format overrides would coexist. Verified reality: dario.cat/mergo v1.0.2 (the exact version GoReleaser v2.18.2 pins, per the release workflow) replaces a non-empty slice under WithOverride, so a base-level dependencies list coexisting with a per-format dependencies override is silently dropped for that format. Runtime dependencies therefore must be declared per format only, and the gate rejects any base-level list.
evidence: local repro: mergo.Merge(&overridden, perFormat, mergo.WithOverride) on base [base] + per-format [perfmt] yielded [perfmt]; goreleaser v2.18.2 internal/pipe/nfpm/nfpm.go mergeOverrides; guarded by TestGoreleaserDeclaresMandatoryRuntimeDependencies (issue #89).

correction: Believed release tags were protected by repository CI gates. Verified reality: the release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml) ran GoReleaser directly on any pushed tag without requiring host-independent or E2E validation gates, allowing broken or unvetted tagged commits to publish releases. Gated GoReleaser on parallel host-independent (`gate`, running `make ci`) and end-to-end (`e2e`, running `make e2e`) jobs with least-privilege permissions, and added regression verification in internal/installcheck.
evidence: Observed in issue #87 and .github/workflows/release.yml; verified by adding TestReleaseWorkflowGatedOnRequiredChecks to internal/installcheck/workflows_test.go.

correction: Believed projectbluefin/website's public/img/logo.svg was the Bluefin brand mark and a usable basis for ChairLift's application icon. Verified reality: that file is the Universal Blue (uBlue) mark, the parent project's logo, not Bluefin's. The site carries no square Bluefin application-icon asset at all: public/favicons/favicon.svg (a raptor head in a circle) is the only square Bluefin mark, public/brands/bluefin*.svg are 2.45:1 horizontal wordmarks, public/brands/universal-blue.svg is a base64 PNG in an SVG wrapper rather than vector, and the 34 files under public/characters/ are horizontal full-body illustrations that are illegible below about 48px. The usable Bluefin-specific icon sources are therefore: the optimized control-center vector logo from delphicmelody/bluefin-graphics for scalable icon use; favicon.svg's raptor-head path for the monochrome symbolic icon; or the #4285f4 'f' ligature isolated from the wordmark (path index 2 of bluefin-wordmark-dark.svg).
evidence: GitHub tree API over projectbluefin/website@main filtered to image blobs; each SVG candidate fetched and inspected for <path> vs <image xlink:href="data:image/png;base64">; all candidates rendered at 128/48/24px via rsvg-convert and compared. Shipped scalable icon derives from delphicmelody/bluefin-graphics (optimized control-center mark); symbolic icon derives from the raptor-head path of website public/favicons/favicon.svg.
impact: Cost two full design rounds in the session that introduced ADR-0012. A future session reading the filename 'logo.svg' will make the same assumption.

correction: Believed failed runs 35179590792 and 35179619278 produced execution logs proving GitHub rejected createComment for lack of issues: write. Verified reality: those runs failed at the workflow/check-suite level with zero jobs and no logs on fork PR reviews; claude-code-review.yml already executes issues.createComment with pull-requests: write. Explicitly declaring issues: write conforms copilot-review-apply.yml to least-privilege practice without relying on unverified failure logs.
evidence: gh api repos/projectbluefin/chairlift/actions/runs/35179590792/jobs returned 0 jobs; issue #141; guarded by TestCopilotReviewApplyWorkflowContract in internal/installcheck/documentation_test.go.

correction: Believed granting issues: write conformed the workflow to least-privilege practice. Verified reality: claude-code-review.yml's publish job (same repo) calls the identical github.rest.issues.createComment against a pull_request issue_number using only contents: read + pull-requests: write, with no issues key at all, and succeeds in production. issues: write was therefore the opposite of least privilege here — it widens the token over the repository's entire issue namespace to cover an endpoint pull-requests: write already satisfies for PR-backed comments.
evidence: Reverted to contents: read + pull-requests: write in 186; TestCopilotReviewApplyWorkflowContract in internal/installcheck/documentation_test.go now forbids issues: write.

correction: Believed signalling a test's private process group and then reaping its leader with cmd.Wait left nothing running. Verified reality: startup's Homebrew readers are grandchildren, so they are reparented to init rather than to the test binary, cmd.Wait never observes them, and they keep creating files under the t.TempDir() used as HOME while Go's cleanup is removing it — the nondeterministic `directory not empty` of issue #91. A test that hands a temporary directory to a process group must drain the group (poll the process table, kill what ignored the signal) from a cleanup registered after t.TempDir(), because cleanups run last-registered-first.
evidence: Reproduced with a leader that backgrounds a writer into its temp dir and exits: os.RemoveAll returned `unlinkat ...: directory not empty` immediately after cmd.Wait, and succeeded after awaitProcessGroupExit (test/e2e/e2e_test.go) reported the surviving member and killed it. Regression coverage: test/e2e/procgroup_test.go.
promoted_to: AGENTS.md (make e2e bullet), docs/design/overview.md CI mirror entry

correction: Believed a failing brew command reports its cause on stderr, so preferring stderr and only falling back to stdout when stderr was empty captured the diagnosis. Verified reality: `brew bundle` runs each entry's real installer with its stderr merged into stdout, buffers that output, and replays it on stdout when the entry fails, while brew's own restatements go to stderr. Because stderr is never empty on a bundle failure, the stdout fallback never fired and the only line naming a cause was discarded. A state-changing brew command's diagnostic must join both streams, stdout first.
evidence: Homebrew/brew Library/Homebrew/bundle.rb Bundle.system: IO.popen(env, [cmd, *args], err: [:child, :out]) ... puts logs.join unless success; Library/Homebrew/bundle/installer.rb:130,325,372,407 print '<verb> <name> has failed!' and '`brew bundle` failed! N Brewfile dependencies failed to install' via $stderr.puts. Issue #140, guarded by TestSummarizeDiagnosticPrefersTheInstallerErrorOverProgress and TestRunBrewCommandAtBoundsMutationOutput/failed_mutation_reports_the_cause_from_either_stream.

correction: Believed a 512x512 avatar PNG trivially fits a 1 MiB ceiling because the uncompressed RGBA raster is exactly 1,048,576 bytes. Verified reality: PNG's one filter byte per scanline makes the raw IDAT stream 512*(2048+1)=1,049,088 bytes before deflate even runs, so content that does not compress can never fit at full size; the 512->384->256 downsample ladder is load-bearing rather than defensive, and at 256 the raw stream is 262,400 bytes — a quarter of the ceiling — so reduction essentially always succeeds while ErrAvatarTooLarge remains the explicit contract for an injected ceiling.
evidence: PNG scanline filter-byte arithmetic (RFC 2083); measured attempt sizes for testdata/katharina.webp through transcodeWebPToPNG on go1.26.6: full-size 236,281 bytes, 384 rung 144,264 bytes, straddling the 184,000-byte constant in TestTranscodeWebPToPNGDownsamplesWhenTheFullSizeEncodeExceedsTheCeiling (internal/avatar/transcode_test.go).

correction: Believed the 1 MiB PNG ceiling bounded the transcoder's work, and that issue #227's 'resize to 512x512' meant scaling the full source bounds. Verified reality: the ceiling only bounds the encoded output, so webp.Decode ran first on unbounded input — a 39-byte VP8L header declaring 16383x16383 parses through webp.DecodeConfig and would force a ~1 GiB NRGBA allocation plus a CatmullRom pass. And the catalog's own artwork is non-square (katharina.webp 440x412, dakota.webp 1392x1070), so scaling full bounds into a square distorts every avatar by up to 23%. An exported io.Reader transcoder must bound input bytes and header-declared pixels before decoding, and crop to a centred square rather than stretch.
evidence: internal/avatar/transcode.go now reads through io.LimitReader(MaxWebPBytes+1) and checks webp.DecodeConfig against MaxSourcePixels before webp.Decode, and scales from centredSquare(src.Bounds()). Coverage: TestTranscodeWebPToPNGRejectsSourcesOverTheInputBounds (crafted 16383x16383 VP8L header returns ErrSourceTooLarge without allocating the frame) and TestTranscodeWebPToPNGCropsNonSquareSourcesInsteadOfStretching in internal/avatar/transcode_test.go.

correction: Believed a dinosaur avatar catalog could be derived mechanically from projectbluefin/website — title-casing the character id for the display name and building `<id>.webp` under public/characters/ for the artwork. Verified reality: three of the ten ids in src/data/wolves-dinosaur-species.ts do not match their artwork filenames (dakotaraptor -> public/characters/dakota.webp, utahraptor -> public/characters/utah.webp, kentrosaurus -> public/characters/header/katharina.webp), so a derived path 404s on exactly those entries; and the project redacts several character names, publishing the literal string '[ Redacted ]' for the Achillobator, Dakotaraptor and Utahraptor characters on docs.projectbluefin.io/dinosaurs. The catalog therefore stores the literal path and the published common name, never a derived one.
evidence: GitHub tree API over projectbluefin/website@92b81281649c0795f16f266f712c9a2798af54c4 filtered to public/characters/*.webp; src/data/wolves-dinosaur-species.ts artwork fields; docs/dinosaurs.md in projectbluefin/documentation. Guarded by TestCatalogPathsAreLiteralRepositoryPaths and TestLookupPathRejectsPathsNoColumnCarries in internal/avatar/avatar_test.go.

correction: Believed issue #228's AccountsService applier could not be written until #227's WebP transcoder landed, because #228 declares 'Blocked by #227'. Verified reality: the applier's entire interface is a uid plus the path of an already-transcoded icon; it neither imports nor names the transcoder, so applier.go compiles and its tests pass on a tree where internal/avatar contains nothing else. #226, #227 and #228 are additive files on one package and can land in any order - #227 only supplies the path at the call site.
evidence: go test ./internal/avatar/... passes with only applier.go and applier_test.go present on upstream/main, as do the vet, gofmt, golangci-lint (0 issues) and both cross-arch builds. The issue's own task list specifies 'SetIconFile s <path>', not any transcoder symbol.

correction: Believed epic #235's developer feed inventory could be lifted into the OPML catalog with a site link (htmlUrl) for every entry. Verified reality: the feed URLs are all live, but the site links are not derivable for six of the shows, and one proposed feed is unusable. openobservability.fm and pureperformance.show do not resolve (DNS NXDOMAIN on 2026-09-22), https://www.heavybit.com/category/library/podcasts/the-kubelist-podcast/ and https://packetpushers.net/series/weekly-podcast/ return HTTP 404, and lwcn.dev (Last Week in Cloud Native) serves a EuroDNS parking page while the epic's only URL for it carried utm_source=bluefin. The catalog therefore omits htmlUrl for OpenObservability Talks, Geeking Out, Agentic DevOps, PurePerformance, The Kubelist Podcast and Argo Unpacked, and excludes LWCN entirely.
evidence: curl -sS -L -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}|%{content_type}' over all 32 xmlUrl values in internal/developerfeeds/developer-feeds.opml returned 200 with an XML content type on 2026-09-22; the same request over candidate htmlUrl values produced NXDOMAIN for openobservability.fm and pureperformance.show and 404 for the Heavybit Kubelist landing page, packetpushers.net/series/weekly-podcast/, akuity.io/podcast/ and geeking-out.castos.com/. Recorded in docs/specs/developer-feeds.md under 'Known exclusions'.
